items.title: Highly Reliable One-Pot SERS Aptasensor for Rapid Cardiac Troponin I Detection in Acute Myocardial Infarction.
items.abstract: Rapid clinical decision-making for acute myocardial infarction (AMI) relies on the timely and precise assessment of cardiac biomarkers. However, detecting cardiac troponin I (cTnI), as the gold-standard biomarker for AMI, with both laboratory-grade sensitivity and rapid clinical turnaround remains a formidable challenge in point-of-care (POC) settings. To address this, we develop a one-pot surface-enhanced Raman scattering (SERS) aptasensor that integrates aptamer-mediated cTnI recognition, catalytic hairpin assembly (CHA) amplification, and plasmonic hotspot assembly. The assay supports two kinetic operating modes within the same assay: a 60-min high-sensitivity mode with a serum limit of detection (LOD) of 53.58 fg/mL and a 20-min rapid-triage mode with an LOD of 14.25 pg/mL, below the clinical decision threshold of 40 pg/mL. In a cohort of 100 clinical serum samples, the bootstrap optimism-corrected diagnostic accuracy was 91.3% for the SERS aptasensor, significantly outperforming conventional ELISA (77.8%). In a subset of 94 subjects with available routine cTnT results, the SERS-cTnI assay achieved an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) of 0.988, comparable to that of the hospital's routine chemiluminescence cTnT assay (0.976), supporting its potential as a complementary diagnostic tool for cTnI-based AMI assessment. Furthermore, compatibility with a handheld Raman spectrometer was evaluated in an independent validation cohort (n = 36), achieving 97.2% accuracy using only 4 μL of serum within 20 min following serum preparation. This reliable one-pot SERS platform bridges ultra-sensitive detection and rapid portable readout, holding promise as a potential tool for future decentralized cardiovascular POC diagnostics.

items.title: Emergency Treatment of Deep Bleeding: A Study on Multifunctional SA/c-PC/PDA@TEMPO Algae Mucilage.
items.abstract: Low survival rates in patients with deep, massive hemorrhage are primarily attributed to three critical challenges: the difficulty of hemostatic dressings reaching the bleeding site, wound infections, and inflammatory reactions triggered by residual materials. To address these issues, this study employed a dual-network crosslinking technique to develop a multifunctional SA/c-PC/PDA@TEMPO algae mucilage. The rheological analysis revealed that the SA/c-PC ratio is the core, affecting the adaptability to irregular wounds and physical hemostatic efficacy of algae mucilage. The results of NIR photothermal performance analysis and antibacterial assays indicated that algae mucilage exhibits outstanding photothermal conversion performances, with temperature rising from room temperature to 50-300 °C within 5 min, which effectively kills bacteria and prevents infections. In vitro cellular experiments confirmed excellent cytocompatibility of algae mucilage, as it supported cell proliferation and metabolism. Moreover, the application of algae mucilage in a rabbit model of femoral artery injury demonstrated that the algae mucilage successfully controls fatal bleeding with 100% survival rate and exhibits c-PC-based anti-inflammatory effect. Overall, the resulting algae mucilage shows translational potential for the emergency treatment of lethal massive bleeding, especially in the case of irregularly deep-penetrating wounds.

items.title: Risk factors associated with in-hospital mortality and a composite of major complications following paediatric congenital cardiac surgery: A systematic review protocol.
items.abstract: Approximately 70% of patients born with congenital heart disease (CHD) require medical or surgical treatment in their first year of life. A reported 90-95% will survive to adulthood due to advances in paediatric cardiology, cardiac surgery and anaesthesia. These reported advances are still not available for over 90% of the children born with CHD in low-and middle-income countries (LMIC). The objectives of this study are to determine the pooled incidence of in-hospital all-cause mortality; identify risk factors associated with in-hospital all-cause mortality and a composite of major complications in paediatric patients undergoing congenital cardiac surgery; and to compare these risk factors between LMICs and high-income countries (HICs). A systematic review will be conducted in accordance with the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) guidelines; this has been registered with PROSPERO 2024 (CRD42024618297). The Population, Exposure and Outcome (PEO) framework will guide the search strategy. Eligible studies will include prospective and retrospective cohort studies, case-control studies, interventional studies and registry/database studies reporting risk factors for in-hospital all-cause mortality and/or major postoperative complications in paediatric patients (≤18 years) undergoing cardiac surgery for CHD. A comprehensive electronic search of PubMed, Scopus, CINAHL, Cochrane Library and Web of Science will identify peer-reviewed English-language studies published from January 2000-2026. Two reviewers will independently screen studies, extract data using a standardised data extraction form, and assess risk of bias using the Newcastle-Ottawa Scale or ROBINS-I, as appropriate to study design. Where appropriate, we will perform random-effects meta-analysis to estimate pooled effect measures and 95% confidence intervals. Statistical heterogeneity will be assessed using the I² statistic, and results will otherwise be synthesised narratively. Where sufficient data are available, risk factors will be compared between LMICs and HICs. In-hospital mortality and major complications following paediatric congenital cardiac surgery are associated with a combination of patient-, surgical- and perioperative risk factors. Identifying these facilitates early risk stratification and optimisation of modifiable risk factors to support targeted perioperative interventions and resource allocation, particularly in LMICs where evidence remains limited. A meta-analysis is not anticipated because of substantial heterogeneity in the study population.

items.title: Molecular types, genetic characteristics and phylogenomic analysis of Staphylococcus aureus causing infective endocarditis.
items.abstract: Staphylococcus aureus is a leading cause of infective endocarditis (IE), yet its molecular epidemiology remains understudied. In this study, genomic data from 285 IE-associated S. aureus strains wre analyzed to inform clinical strategies. Strains were characterized by multilocus sequence typing (MLST), spa typing, and SCCmec classification. Antibiotic resistance genes (ARGs) and virulence factors (VFs) were identified from genomic data, and phylogenetic trees were constructed. Predominant sequence types (STs) included ST45 (CC45), ST5 (CC5), ST8 (CC8), ST15 (CC15), ST30 (CC30), ST1 (CC1), and ST188 (CC1). Common spa types were t2, t8, t230, and t88. Among 46 mecA-positive strains, SCCmec IV (50%) and II (34.8%) predominated. MecA was more prevalent in ST5 and ST8 strains but less prevalent in ST45 and ST15 strains. ST45 strains lacked splA, splB, and splE, unlike other STs. ST45 and ST8 strains harbored higher numbers of ARGs, while ST15 and ST188 carried fewer ARGs. Similarly, ST5 and ST1 strains exhibited higher VF counts than ST15 and ST188 strains. Phylogenetic tree revealed that some clades dominated by a single ST contained insertions of strains from different STs, and closely related strains were primarily associated with different CC groups. Some CC1 and CC8 strains clustered together on a branch, indicating a close genetic relationship. ST5 and ST8 clones pose high ARG or VF risks and warrant targeted therapy, whereas ST15 and ST188 may represent lower-risk lineages. The prevalence of SCCmec IV highlights the contribution of community-associated MRSA to IE. Phylogenetic inconsistencies reflect adaptive evolution of S. aureus in IE.
items.journal: Journal of infection in developing countries

items.title: Computed Tomography-Derived Left Atrial Intramyocardial Fat and Low-Voltage Zones in Atrial Fibrillation.
items.abstract: Left atrial low-voltage zones (LVZs) are associated with atrial fibrosis and arrhythmia recurrence after atrial fibrillation (AF) ablation and are thought to underlie many recurrences despite durable pulmonary vein isolation. However, noninvasive markers of the arrhythmogenic atrial substrate remain poorly characterized. We sought to investigate the association between computed tomography (CT)-derived left atrial intramyocardial fat (inFAT) and electroanatomically defined LVZs. In this single-center retrospective study, 145 consecutive patients undergoing first-time radiofrequency AF ablation underwent preprocedural dual-source CT and high-density left atrial voltage mapping in sinus rhythm. LVZs were defined as contiguous regions with bipolar voltage 2 ; p < 0.001). Patients with LVZs also demonstrated larger volumes of total inFAT, dense inFAT, and fat-myocardial admixture, accompanied by lower radiodensity values of total and dense inFAT. In multivariable logistic regression analysis, persistent AF (adjusted odds ratio [OR]: 5.389; 95% confidence interval [CI]: 2.162-13.433; p < 0.001) and dense inFAT volume (adjusted OR: 3.439; 95% CI: 1.107-10.677; p = 0.033) remained independently associated with the presence of LVZs, whereas LAVi did not. Among the CT-derived fat metrics, only dense inFAT retained an independent association with LVZs after adjustment for clinical covariates. CT-derived dense inFAT was independently associated with left atrial LVZs and may represent a novel noninvasive marker of the arrhythmogenic atrial substrate in AF. Prospective studies are warranted to determine its role in substrate-guided ablation strategies and risk stratification.

items.title: HPV knowledge and willingness to vaccinate among unvaccinated female college students: A cross-sectional comparison between a comprehensive university and a health vocational college in Fujian, China.
items.abstract: Cervical cancer remains a significant burden in China, and HPV vaccination is key to prevention. Female college students are a crucial target, yet knowledge and willingness may vary across institution types. To compare HPV knowledge and vaccination willingness between female students from a comprehensive university and a health vocational college, and identify associated factors. A cross-sectional study was conducted from May to June 2026 among 2,761 female undergraduate students (first- and second-year) recruited from one comprehensive university and one health vocational college in Fujian, China. An electronic questionnaire collected data on demographic characteristics, HPV knowledge, vaccination willingness, vaccine preferences, and reasons for unwillingness. The overall HPV vaccination willingness rate was 78.7% (2,173/2,761). The mean HPV knowledge score was 6.17 ± 2.66 (out of 10), with only 37.0%(1,021/2,761) achieving high knowledge. Non-healthcare majors scored higher than healthcare majors (6.28 vs. 5.97, p  = .003). Six independent factors were identified: healthcare major (OR = 0.65), higher income (OR = 0.58), maternal vaccination (OR = 2.28), friend vaccination (OR = 1.89), sexual history (OR = 1.74), and higher knowledge (middle level OR = 1.80; high level OR = 2.02). Among willing participants, 66.3% (1,441/2,173) preferred the nonavalent vaccine, and 56.1% (1,218/2,173) were unsure about domestic vs. imported vaccines. Main reasons for unwillingness were adverse reaction concerns, cost, and a wait-and-see attitude. HPV vaccination willingness was relatively high among unvaccinated female college students in Fujian, China, but knowledge gaps persisted, particularly regarding the recommended vaccination age. Willingness was significantly associated with academic major, household income, social influences, and knowledge level. Targeted educational interventions, financial support, and peer-based strategies are needed.

items.title: The "ever-vaccinated" stock-flow bias in adult RSV vaccine policy evaluation: A methodological caution and a flow-based remedy.
items.abstract: Adult respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) vaccines are recommended as a single dose without routine revaccination; cumulative "ever-vaccinated" coverage is therefore a stock variable rising mechanically each season. Prior guidance implies this stock-flow distinction, yet no study has provided a portable, instrument-agnostic remedy or quantified this decomposition for the 2025-26 season. Using weekly 2025-26 U.S. National Immunization Survey data, we decomposed cumulative coverage into a prior-season stock and current-season flow, approximating the stock by the season-opening estimate. As of the latest available 2025-26 data (week ending 2026-02-21; mid-season snapshot), 84.9% of coverage among adults 75+ (43.2%) and 82.9% among high-risk adults 50-74 (32.8%) was attributable to prior-season stock - only 15-17% reflected current-season behavior; this stock share is an empirical approximation, not an exact decomposition. In two exploratory region-level quasi-experiments, the flow metric showed no sustained uptake acceleration (all primary tests p  ≥ .19; a transient early-season gap, p  = .008 post hoc, did not persist); these underpowered analyses are illustrative only, not identified for the policy effect. To our knowledge, this is the first portable flow-metric operationalization for survey and registry data, released as open code. Registry data exploratorily show the stock metric can obscure equity monitoring (Gini 0.210→0.202; range 39.7→43.5 pp; not significant). As a mid-season snapshot, these figures are an upper bound on the end-of-season value; the conclusion that coverage is dominated by prior-season stock holds through the season. RSV policy evaluation should pre-specify current-season flow as the primary outcome and report the stock share as a strongly recommended diagnostic.

items.title: Tuning the immune ecosystem to treat cancer.
items.abstract: Engineering the immune cell milieu around tumors could make them more sensitive to immunotherapy.

items.title: Differentiation of stem-like CD4 + T cells modulates early effector responses in colorectal cancer.
items.abstract: Strategies to improve cancer immunotherapy have largely focused on the intratumor immunosuppressive microenvironment, whereas approaches to amplify peripheral T cells and promote tumor recruitment have not been thoroughly explored. Using imaging mass cytometry in patients with colorectal cancer (CRC), we observed T helper 1 (T H 1)-like immune architectures in mismatch repair-deficient tumors associated with response to anti-programmed cell death protein 1 (PD-1) immunotherapy. By contrast, mismatch repair-proficient (pMMR) tumors showed regulatory T-dominant spatial interactions. Clonal analyses revealed that stem-like CD4 + T cells differentiated into T H 1-like cells after PD-1 blockade. In pMMR CRC mouse models, combined OX40 agonist and PD-1 blockade suppressed tumor progression by expanding Il7r + early effector CD4 + intermediates in tumor-draining lymph nodes, promoting migration and connection with T H 1-like cells. This was accompanied by interferon-γ-dependent induction of immunostimulatory monocyte-macrophages and CD8 + effector T cells. These findings suggest that leveraging peripheral CD4 + T cell amplification may improve immunotherapy responses.

items.title: Generation and in vitro functional characterization of anti-CD22 chimeric antigen receptor T cells derived from newly generated monoclonal antibody clones.
items.abstract: Chimeric antigen receptor (CAR) T-cell therapy has transformed the treatment of B-cell malignancies, but relapse after CD19-directed therapy remains a major challenge, often because of loss or downregulation of CD19 expression. CD22 is an attractive alternative target because it is expressed on malignant B cells, including in many cases of CD19-negative disease. In this study, we generated and characterized novel anti-CD22 monoclonal antibody-derived CAR constructs for in vitro evaluation. Four anti-CD22 monoclonal antibody clones were initially screened, and two clones, 24A7G6 and 29H9C8, were selected for CAR development based on their favorable binding and CAR surface expression profiles. Second-generation CAR constructs containing either a 4-1BB or CD28 costimulatory domain were generated and introduced into primary human T cells. The resulting CAR T cells were evaluated for expansion, immunophenotype, activation and inhibitory marker expression, cytokine secretion, short-term cytotoxicity, long-term co-culture activity, and sequential tumor rechallenge against CD22-positive Raji and Nalm-6 cells and CD22-negative K562 cells. Both 24A7G6- and 29H9C8-derived CAR T cells expanded efficiently, showed predominant CD8 + populations with naïve and central memory phenotypes, and mediated potent antigen-specific cytotoxicity against CD22-positive target cells, while showing no activity against CD22-negative cells. Following antigen stimulation, CAR T cells upregulated activation markers and showed modest increases in inhibitory receptors. In long-term co-culture and sequential rechallenge assays, all constructs retained antitumor activity under prolonged antigen exposure. Notably, the 24A7G6-CD28 CAR demonstrated enhanced sustained tumor control compared with the corresponding 4-1BB construct in extended assays, whereas short-term cytotoxicity was broadly comparable across constructs. These findings show that the newly generated 24A7G6 and 29H9C8 scFvs can function as effective targeting domains for CD22-directed CAR T-cell development and provide an in vitro basis for prioritizing lead constructs for further preclinical evaluation.

items.title: Serum isthmin-1 levels in chronic hepatitis B: association with viral replication and hepatic dysfunction.
items.abstract: Chronic hepatitis B virus (HBV) infection remains a major global health problem, underscoring the need for biomarkers that reflect viral replication and liver function. Isthmin-1 (ISM-1), an immunometabolic adipokine, has not been adequately studied in chronic HBV infection. This study evaluated serum ISM-1 levels in patients with chronic HBV to assess its potential as a complementary marker of viral activity and hepatic dysfunction. In this cross-sectional study, 100 patients with histologically mild chronic hepatitis B and 60 healthy controls were enrolled. Serum ISM-1 levels were measured using a commercial enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA) kit alongside comprehensive virological and biochemical assessments. Serum ISM-1 concentrations were significantly lower in patients with chronic HBV than in healthy controls (102.74 ± 15.64 vs. 194.62 ± 187.59 pg/mL; p < 0.001). ISM-1 levels demonstrated a significant downward trend as HBV DNA categories increased (p = 0.001), indicating an inverse relationship with viral replication. Multiple linear regression identified direct bilirubin as a positive independent predictor of ISM-1 levels. ROC analysis showed moderate overall performance (AUC = 0.656); the marker exhibited a remarkably high sensitivity (97.0%) but limited specificity (38.7%). Serum ISM-1 levels are significantly reduced in chronic HBV infection and are inversely associated with viral replication. The positive correlation with direct bilirubin may reflect an adaptive cellular response to hepatocellular stress rather than simple dysfunction. Despite its limited specificity, the high sensitivity of ISM-1 suggests that it could be a valuable complementary tool for monitoring disease progression and viral status in clinical practice.
items.journal: Journal of infection in developing countries

items.title: Hepatitis B surface antigen prevalence among people living with HIV in a tertiary hospital in Lagos, Nigeria.
items.abstract: Human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) and hepatitis B virus (HBV) share transmission routes and may interact synergistically, accelerating liver disease and worsening HIV outcomes. This study assessed the prevalence and serological pattern of HBV infection among people living with HIV attending a tertiary health facility in Lagos, Nigeria, providing local evidence to inform integrated screening and prevention strategies. A cross-sectional study was conducted among 200 HIV-positive individuals aged 16-65 years attending a tertiary healthcare facility in Lagos, Nigeria, between January and June 2023. Participants recruited included 31 males and 169 females. Samples were screened for hepatitis B surface antigen (HBsAg) using a rapid immunochromatographic test strip. Additional markers (HBsAb, HBeAg, HBeAb, HBcAb) were assessed among HBsAg-positive individuals. Associations were tested using chi-square analysis with significance at p < 0.05, and prevalence estimates were reported with 95% confidence intervals. HBV/HIV co-infection prevalence was 5.5% (11/200; 95% CI: 2.3-8.7). Co-infection was higher among males, 8.2% (5/61), than among females, 3.6% (6/139), but the difference was not significant (χ² = 1.228, p = 0.268). Highest prevalence occurred among those aged 25-29 years (22.2%; 2/9) and 45-49 years (13.2%; 5/38), although age was not significantly associated with HBsAg positivity (χ² = 13.44, p = 0.062). Among HBsAg-positive participants tested with additional markers (n = 6), HBeAb was detected in four individuals. Dual profiles included HBeAg + HBeAb and HBeAb + HBcAb (each 16.7%). HBV/HIV coinfection persists in this population, highlighting the need for routine HBV screening, vaccination, and integrated care programs.
items.journal: Journal of infection in developing countries

items.title: Impact of alcohol use discontinuation on adipose tissue insulin resistance among Latino patients with and without underlying chronic liver disease.
items.abstract: We evaluated the effect of short-term moderate alcohol discontinuation on adipose tissue insulin resistance (adipo-IR) and factors associated with its change in Latinos with and without hepatitis C virus (HCV). Nondiabetic Latino adults without (N = 17) or with (N = 7) HCV underwent clinical, laboratory, genetic, and metabolic testing. Metabolic testing was repeated after 6.5 weeks of moderate alcohol discontinuation. Adipo-IR was measured using a 2-step insulin suppression test. Multivariable linear regression, including HCV status, identified factors associated with change in adipo-IR. Median age was 50 years, 58% female, median BMI 26.3 kg/m². Genetic ancestry was 57% European, 36% Native American, and 3.5% African. CYP2E1 genotyping showed 14% were homozygous for [c2/c2] risk-allele. No significant changes in adipo-IR occurred after alcohol discontinuation. On multivariable regression, CYP2E1 homozygous risk-allele (vs. none, estimate 0.25 mmol/L, p < 0.001) and overweight/obesity (vs. normal weight, estimate 0.13 mmol/L, p = 0.02), but not HCV, were associated with change in adipo-IR following alcohol discontinuation. Although there was no significant overall change in adipo-IR following short-term moderate alcohol discontinuation, CYP2E1 homozygous risk-allele and overweight/obesity were associated with changes in adipo-IR. These exploratory findings suggest that host genetic and metabolic characteristics may influence metabolic responses to alcohol discontinuation and warrant validation in larger prospective studies.

items.title: Microfluidic platform for rapid passive preparation of complex biological matrices in point-of-care testing.
items.abstract: Efficient whole blood processing at the point-of-care (POC) remains challenging due to interference from cellular components, risk of hemolysis, as well as reliance on external equipment and skilled operators. Here, we present a passive, low-cost microfluidic platform for rapid separation of cellular components from diluted samples of whole blood without the need for external pumps. The device features a circular maze-shaped microchannel incorporating 18 sequential wells, enabling effective cell retention through purely passive hydrodynamic mechanisms. Fabricated from hydrophilic polymer sheets and pressure-sensitive adhesive (PSA) layers, the platform is scalable, disposable, and enables very low-cost production (< $1 per unit). The blood-separation performance of the standalone microfluidic chip was validated using HEK-293 and AtT-20 cell suspensions, mixed cell suspensions, and diluted human blood. Efficient retention of cellular components in the early wells generated a cell-free filtrate suitable for downstream analytical applications. Building on this validated separation capability, the platform was integrated with a lateral flow immunoassay (LFIA) module as a proof-of-concept in a POC application by testing for hepatitis B surface antigen (HBsAg). The integrated system enabled detection of HBsAg at concentrations as low as 10 ng/mL within 10 min. In addition, deep learning-assisted convolutional neural networks were employed for automated assessment of filtration efficiency and test-line intensity. Overall, this work demonstrates a robust and accessible microfluidic sample-preparation platform with potential for decentralized diagnostic applications, particularly critical for resource-limited settings.

items.title: HIV Treatment and Program Preferences Among Ryan White Clients in New York City in the Era of Long-Acting Injectable ART: A Discrete Choice Experiment.
items.abstract: Despite improvements in treatment for people living with HIV (PWH), adherence remains a challenge for many. We aimed to identify preferences for daily pill or long-acting injectable (LAI) antiretroviral therapy (ART) and treatment package features among PWH enrolled in Ryan White HIV/AIDS Program Part A (RWPA) Medical Case Management (MCM) programs. Participants were recruited from six MCM programs in the New York RWPA eligible metropolitan area. We developed a discrete choice experiment (DCE) with four attributes: (1) Type of ART Medication (daily pills/LAI), (2) Service Location and Mode, (3) Support, and (4) Rewards. Latent class multinomial logit analysis (LCA) was used for preference estimation and hypothesis-free investigation of preference heterogeneity. June 2022-January 2023, 200 New York RWPA MCM clients completed the DCE. In the two-group LCA solution, a majority of participants preferred LAI regimens over daily pills (n = 114 [57%] versus n = 86 [43%]). Those preferring LAI ART were younger (χ 2  = 16.4, p  2  = 4.38, p  2  = 7.05, p < 0.01). Only 4.5% of participants self-reported having tried LAI ART. Our study found groups of participants with different ART regimen preferences, and limited familiarity with LAI ART. To inform regimen selection, we developed educational materials and a patient-provider decision-making tool. A pesar de los avances en el tratamiento para las personas que viven con el VIH (PVVIH), la adherencia sigue siendo un desafío para muchas de ellas. Nuestro objetivo fue identificar las preferencias entre pastillas diarias o inyectables de acción prolongada (IAP) para terapia antirretroviral (TAR), así como las características del paquete de tratamiento, entre las PVVIH inscritas en los programas de gestión de casos médicos (GCM) de la parte A del programa Ryan White HIV/AIDS (RWPA). Los participantes fueron reclutados de seis programas de GCM dentro del área metropolitana de Nueva York elegible para el RWPA. Diseñamos un experimento de elección discreta (EED) con cuatro atributos: (1) tipo de medicamento antirretroviral (pastillas diarias/IAP), (2) ubicación y modalidad del servicio, (3) apoyo, y (4) incentivos. Se utilizó un análisis de clases latentes (ACL) de tipo logit multinomial para estimar las preferencias e investigar, sin hipótesis previas, la heterogeneidad de dichas preferencias. Entre junio 2022 y enero 2023, 200 usuarios de los programas de GCM del RWPA en Nueva York completaron el EED. En la solución de ACL de dos grupos, la mayoría de los participantes prefirió los regímenes de IAP a las pastillas diarias (n = 114 [57%] frente a n = 86 [43%]). Aquellos que preferían la TAR con IAP eran más jóvenes (χ 2  = 16,4, p  2  = 4,38, p  2  = 7,05, p < 0,01). Solo el 4,5% de los participantes informaron haber probado la TAR con IAP. Nuestro estudio identificó grupos de participantes con distintas preferencias de régimen antirretroviral y un conocimiento limitado sobre la TAR con IAP. Para facilitar la elección del régimen, desarrollamos materiales educativos y una herramienta paciente-proveedor para la toma de decisiones.

items.title: NMR-based metabolomic profiling reveals distinct metabolic signatures of primary hepatocytes and hepatocellular carcinoma cell lines.
items.abstract: Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) is characterized by profound metabolic reprogramming that supports tumor initiation, growth, and metastasis. Understanding how metabolic profiles differ between normal hepatocytes and HCC cells with distinct aggressive phenotypes may help identify metabolic features associated with tumor progression. The Dt81Hepa1-6 cell line, derived from the murine Hepa1-6 hepatoma line, exhibits increased aggressiveness and provides a useful model for investigating metabolic features associated with aggressive behavior. We performed an integrative 1H NMR-based metabolomic analysis of intracellular extracts (endometabolome) and extracellular culture media (exometabolome) from primary hepatocytes, Hepa1-6, and Dt81Hepa1-6 cells collected at 24h and 48h. Multivariate statistical analyses, including PCA and PLS-DA, were used to characterize metabolic differences among the three cell types. Metabolic profiling revealed a clear separation between primary hepatocytes and HCC cells in both endometabolomic and exometabolomic datasets. HCC cells exhibited increased lactate and alanine levels together with decreased intracellular glucose and glutathione, consistent with altered glycolytic and redox metabolism. Time-dependent changes in glucose consumption and lactate release were prominent in extracellular media from both HCC cell lines. The aggressive Dt81Hepa1-6 line displayed a distinct metabolic phenotype characterized by increased extracellular pyroglutamate, citrate, formate and particularly BCAA-derived ketoacids, 2-oxo-isovalerate and 3-methyl-2-oxovalerate. These findings are consistent with alterations in BCAA-associated metabolism, glutamine/glutamate, and TCA-related metabolism in the more aggressive cell line. Overall, the integration of endometabolomic and exometabolomic 1H NMR profiling identifies metabolic features associated with the aggressive phenotype of Dt81Hepa1-6 cells. BCAA-derived ketoacids, pyroglutamate, and TCA-related metabolites emerge as candidate metabolic features that warrant validation in additional experimental and clinical HCC models.

items.title: Epigenetic regulation of DOT1L methyltransferase activityremodels lipid metabolism to alleviate ferroptosis-induced liver injury.
items.abstract: Epigenetic modifications contribute to lipid-related disorders by modulating the expression of key genes involved in lipid metabolism. Accumulating evidence suggests that lipid metabolism-mediated ferroptosis drives the progression of metabolic associated steatohepatitis (MASH) and liver injury. However, whether epigenetic mechanisms remodel lipid metabolism to regulate ferroptosis-induced liver damage remains unclear. Here, through pharmacological screening of epigenetics-related compounds and CRISPR-Cas9-based screening targeting epigenetic factors, we identified DOT1 Like Histone Lysine Methyltransferase (DOT1L) as a key sensitizer of hepatocytes to ferroptosis and subsequent liver injury, whereas inhibition of DOT1L reverses the phenomenon. DOT1L loss remodeled the phospholipid landscape by decreasing PUFA-containing phospholipids while increasing monounsaturated and lysophospholipid species. Mechanistically, DOT1L depletion reduced H3K79me1 and H3K79me2 occupancy at the PLA2G7, ALDH3B1, and PLCXD3 loci, particularly across gene-body regions, while increasing promoter-proximal accessibility and expression of these phospholipid-remodeling genes. These genes suppress ferroptosis by reducing the levels of phospholipids containing polyunsaturated fatty acids (PL-PUFAs). Furthermore, we demonstrated that AMPK phosphorylates DOT1L at Ser786, weakens its association with AF9, and suppresses H3K79 methyltransferase activity and ferroptosis sensitivity. Collectively, our findings reveal the AMPK-DOT1L-H3K79 methylation axis as a novel lipid metabolic pathway that regulates ferroptosis and maintains hepatic homeostasis, offering new therapeutic insights for ferroptosis-related liver injury.

items.title: Premature immune aging in obesity: a testable framework linking immunosenescence, metaflammation, and multiorgan dysfunction.
items.abstract: Obesity is a chronic immunometabolic disorder associated with alterations in biological aging pathways and increased risks of type 2 diabetes mellitus, cardiovascular disease, metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease, chronic kidney disease, neurodegeneration, and cancer. Obesity and chronological aging share several characteristics, including low-grade inflammation, cellular senescence, mitochondrial dysfunction, oxidative stress, epigenetic alterations, and immune remodeling. However, these similarities do not necessarily establish accelerated biological immune aging. This review critically evaluates obesity-associated immunosenescence, metaflammation, and multiorgan dysfunction by examining supporting and conflicting findings, alternative explanations, methodological limitations, and therapeutic evidence. Although experimental and observational studies report alterations in lymphocyte differentiation, innate immune function, inflammatory signaling, and selected biological-age markers, these findings are not uniformly observed across immune-cell populations, tissues, or metabolic phenotypes. Metabolically healthy obesity, tissue-dependent epigenetic aging, and differences between human and animal findings challenge the interpretation of obesity as a universal accelerator of immunosenescence. Furthermore, chronological age, cytomegalovirus infection, sex-related differences, adiposity distribution, and metabolic comorbidities complicate attributing immune alterations specifically to obesity. The proposed immunosenescence-metaflammation-multiorgan dysfunction framework therefore remains a testable mechanistic hypothesis rather than an established causal pathway. Although immune-cell phenotypes, epigenetic clocks, inflammatory mediators, and multi-omics signatures may help characterize obesity-associated immune dysfunction, their specificity, longitudinal validity, and clinical utility remain insufficiently established. Nutritional interventions, exercise, bariatric surgery, and pharmacological treatments can improve selected metabolic and inflammatory outcomes, but these improvements do not necessarily demonstrate sustained reversal of biological immune aging. By critically comparing supportive evidence with contradictory observations and unresolved causal relationships, this review identifies the principal limitations of current mechanistic, biomarker, and therapeutic research. Future studies should prioritize longitudinal immune profiling, direct functional assessment, tissue- and sex-specific analyses, causal validation, and controlled interventions incorporating validated immune-aging endpoints to determine whether premature immune aging is a measurable and therapeutically modifiable consequence of obesity.

items.title: 5'tRF-32-Glu promotes hepatocellular carcinoma progression and has diagnostic value in serum.
items.abstract: To assess the diagnostic relevance of serum 5'tRF-32-Glu and its potential role to hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) progression. High-throughput sequencing of paired HCC and non-tumor tissues was used to identify candidate transfer RNA-derived small RNAs. Serum 5'tRF-32-Glu was subsequently quantified by reverse transcription quantitative polymerase chain reaction, and its molecular identity was verified by agarose gel electrophoresis and Sanger sequencing. Diagnostic performance and associations with clinicopathological features were assessed in a clinical cohort, including analyses of HCC, healthy controls, hepatitis controls, and BCLC 0/A HCC. Its effects on HCC cell proliferation, migration, invasion, and xenograft growth were examined in vitro and in vivo. Serum 5'tRF-32-Glu levels were higher in the HCC group than in healthy controls and patients with hepatitis, whereas surgical resection was accompanied by a marked reduction in circulating levels. Higher serum expression was associated with tumor size, tumor number, BCLC stage, and Child-Pugh class. The area under the receiver operating characteristic curve for 5'tRF-32-Glu was 0.714, and combining it with alpha-fetoprotein and protein induced by vitamin K absence or antagonist-II increased the area under the curve to 0.884 and the sensitivity increased to 96%. Functionally, 5'tRF-32-Glu promoted HCC cell proliferation, migration, and invasion, while its inhibition suppressed xenograft growth. Serum 5'tRF-32-Glu shows potential as a circulating HCC biomarker and may complement established markers for improved detection. Its functional effects on malignant phenotypes further support its potential role in the progress of HCC.

items.title: Discovery of Orally Effective Corydamine Derivatives Targeting Glutathione Metabolism to Sensitize Hepatocellular Carcinoma to Sorafenib.
items.abstract: Sorafenib offers limited benefit in hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC). In this study, we designed and synthesized a series of novel corydamine derivatives and identified 8g as a lead compound with anti-HCC activity comparable to sorafenib. Mechanistic studies suggest that 8g targets glutathione reductase (GR), disrupting glutathione metabolism and NADPH homeostasis and weakening tumor redox defenses. Notably, the combination of 8g and sorafenib markedly enhanced ROS generation, inhibited HCC cell migration and invasion, and induced G2/M arrest and apoptosis, demonstrating strong synergistic anticancer activity. In addition, 8g showed favorable druggability, including good metabolic stability in human liver microsomes (T1/2 > 5 h), low hERG inhibition (IC50 > 50 μM), and high oral bioavailability (84.9%). In a Huh7 xenograft model, the combination achieved 61.0% tumor growth inhibition, significantly outperforming sorafenib alone (29.7%). These findings propose a redox-targeting strategy to sensitize HCC to sorafenib and highlight 8g as a promising anti-HCC lead.
